neighbours.label: a participle of physical disturbance in 'when crushed / broken / shaken': handling an object that releases a response
fire: The leaves of lemon balm give off a sharp citrus smell when crushed between the fingers.
This mushroom turns deep blue within seconds when bruised or cut.
Dandelion stems ooze a bitter white sap when snapped in half.
The seed pods split open and fling their seeds when touched.
Some beetles release a foul-smelling liquid when disturbed by predators.
A maraca makes its rattling sound when shaken back and forth.
The root releases a strong onion odour when scraped with a knife.
Mimosa leaflets fold up quickly when brushed by a hand.
quiet: The leaves of lemon balm give off a sharp citrus smell on warm summer evenings.
This mushroom turns deep blue within a few days of being picked.
Dandelion stems contain a bitter white sap that is rich in latex.
The seed pods split open and release their seeds in late autumn.
Some beetles release a foul-smelling liquid that keeps predators away.
A maraca is a rattle made from a dried gourd filled with seeds.
The root has a strong onion odour and is often used in soups.
Mimosa leaflets fold up quickly at night and open again at dawn.
